title.narrative: Provision of live-saving WASH intervention to reduce the humanitarian impact of the predicted La Nina on the most affected communities in Wanlaweyn district of lower Shabelle region, southwest state.

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia is expected to continue facing climatic events like droughts, floods, conflict, insecurity, and disease outbreaks in 2024, driving humanitarian needs across the country. The 2024 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) indicates that 6.9 million people will require humanitarian assistance, with 3.6 million facing crisis levels of hunger from July to September 2024. This number is expected to rise to 4.4 million between October and December 2024 as drought conditions worsen due to below-average rainfall. Moreover, 1.7 million children under the age of five are projected to face acute malnutrition by July 2025, and more than half of the population remains water insecure. Access to health care is severely limited, exacerbating vulnerability to preventable diseases and compounding the alarming levels of malnutrition in the country.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtTlt/spangtltspangthe proposed STS project aims to provide critical WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) interventions to support 16,000 individuals in the Wanlaweyn district, including vulnerable IDP (Internally Displaced Persons) settlements and host communities. These areas are particularly at risk due to La Niña, which is expected to worsen drought conditions, malnutrition, and limited access to health and WASH services. The project will mitigate the impacts of La Niña by focusing on water access, sanitation, hygiene promotion, and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA).lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtKey WASH InterventionsltbrgtWater Access and Infrastructure:ltbrgtRehabilitation of two strategic deep wells, one borehole using a hybrid system (solar-powered with diesel backup).Construction of five water kiosks connected via a piping system in IDP settlements. Refurbishment of water tanks and engine rooms for sustainable water storage. Training and Capacity Building, water quality monitoring and treatment through chlorination and provision of essential spare parts for strategic boreholes and deep wells:ltbrgtTraining of 3 gender balanced management committees in water treatment and monitoring to ensure sustainable water management in vulnerable IDP communities. Construction of 62 latrines, including 10 accessible latrines for people with disabilities, purchase and distribution of 310 potable solar lamps for 310 families that will benefit from latrine construction exercise. Training of 20 Community Hygiene Promoters to conduct household visits and institutional outreach. Purchase and distribution of 1,300 hygiene kits, including menstrual hygiene management (MHM) supplies, for malnourished children and pregnant or lactating women. Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA):ltbrgtTraining of 20 staff members on PSEA to ensure protection measures are integrated into WASH services. To achieve sectoral integration STS close work with the Federal Ministry of Health (FMOH), Health, Nutrition partners , district local authority, Health and Nutrition cluster partners operating in Wanlaweyn to get other complementarity for achieving full integration packages through referrals, collaborations and robust coordination both at Lower Shabelle regional authorities and national/regional WASH clusters. This approach ensures a multi-sectoral response that integrates efforts across Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Protection sectors, providing a comprehensive and efficient solution to the community’s needs. This project aims to provide life-saving WASH services, improve sanitation infrastructure, promote better hygiene practices, and safeguard vulnerable populations from abuse. The multi-sectoral integration ensures a holistic response, addressing water insecurity, malnutrition, and health care challenges in a sustainable and dignified manner.ltbrgtProject targeted locations will be the following site including both Wanla Weyne IDPs and rural villages ( Tabelaha, Eribka, Dudumey, Yaqdhub, Hero, Hawal filey, Xero, Balow,Doonlka)ltbrgtlt/pgt
